comments.note: IntDecimalConverter.ConvertBack: the `value is not decimal d` guard handles both null and non-null non-decimal inputs identically. Tests cover both null-to-int and null-to-int? paths but do not add a dedicated test for a non-null non-decimal value (e.g., a string). Since NumericUpDown only ever returns decimal? in normal Avalonia usage, this is a negligible gap in practice.

FakeMovieRepository.GetOriginalFilenameAsync respects the existing _exception guard via Throw<Task<string?>>(), so the error path is structurally consistent — but there is no test exercising the exception path for this method. Not a blocker given scope of WP-005.

summary: Code review PASS. All three files reviewed line-by-line. One Fix-Forward applied: moved _originalFilename field and SetOriginalFilename() from the IMovieRepository implementation section into the Configuration section of FakeMovieRepository.cs, consistent with the established _movie/SetMovie and _exception/SetException grouping pattern. Build confirmed clean after fix. IntDecimalConverterTests.cs and the two new MovieEditorViewModelTests additions are clean with no issues.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied to tests/VideoIndexer.App.Tests/TestHelpers/FakeMovieRepository.cs: moved `private string? _originalFilename` field and `SetOriginalFilename(string? filename)` method from inside the `// IMovieRepository implementation` region up to the private fields block and `// Configuration` section respectively. This restores the established pattern where all pre-load state fields (`_movie`, `_exception`, `_originalFilename`) are grouped at the top of the class and all configuration setters (`SetMovie`, `SetException`, `SetOriginalFilename`) are co-located in the Configuration section. Non-behavioral — build confirmed clean after the move.

[documentation-forward] The class-level XML doc on FakeMovieRepository currently reads: 'Supports pre-loading a movie (SetMovie), tracking call counts, and simulating faulted tasks (SetException).' It should also mention SetOriginalFilename now that a third pre-load helper has been added, to keep the summary accurate for future contributors.

IntDecimalConverterTests.cs correctly covers all production branches: 3 Convert paths (int, null, non-int) and all 4 ConvertBack paths (decimal→int, null→int, null→int?, decimal→int?). The singleton Sut pattern is appropriate given the stateless converter design.
MoveActorDown_IsNoOp_WhenNoActorSelected mirrors MoveActorUp_IsNoOp_WhenNoActorSelected exactly in structure — a deliberate symmetry that makes the test set easy to reason about.

CleanLabel_CallsGetOriginalFilenameAsync test correctly verifies three distinct behaviors in one AAA block: (1) GetOriginalFilenameAsync was invoked once, (2) label cleaner Show was called once, (3) RawFilename received the path stem 'My Cool Movie'. Multiple related assertions on a single Act are idiomatic here and do not violate single-responsibility for tests.
